A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same benchmarking study. All 37 pages of v1 and 42 pages of v2, including their figures, tables, equations and appendices, support reliable comparison despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmarking experiments, controlled synthetic-scene evaluations and camera-pose correction experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original rotational camera-pose noise experiments in Appendix B.3.

M1.justification: No implemented algorithmic revision is established. The shared implementation, losses and procedures in Appendix C are retained. The revised STG overview wording and Appendix F's discussion of regularization do not document changes to the implemented methods.

E1.justification: The five benchmark datasets and synthetic cube scenes are retained. Appendix B.3 adds a noisy-input scenario by deliberately perturbing camera poses for existing non-rotating cube sequences.

E2.justification: Corresponding benchmark and pose-correction comparisons retain the same methods, including TiNeuVox, 3DGS, EffGS, both STG variants, DeformableGS, 4DGS and RTGS. The new noise study uses existing Gaussian methods; newly cited regularization approaches are not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 introduces uniform rotational perturbations U[-alpha, alpha] with alpha equal to 1 or 5 degrees, compared with clean poses on non-rotating cubes. Section 3.3 also changes STG's stated third-order basis from polynomial to radial basis, without a corresponding implementation update in Appendix C.

E4.justification: v2 retains v1's HyperNeRF pose-correction analysis and synthetic-motion ablations, adding a focused controlled pose-noise sensitivity study. Tables 10–11 and Figures 40–41 examine quality degradation, ranking stability and reconstruction artifacts.

E5.justification: Both versions already report three independent optimizations, standard deviations and error bars. v2 explicitly explains that bars show means with error bars extending one standard deviation; this clarifies the existing practice without establishing additional runs or a changed statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables and figure results are retained. Appendix B.3 adds noise-condition results: Table 11 reports DeformableGS PSNR of 29.41, 24.92 and 24.66 dB for 0-, 1- and 5-degree perturbations. These are newly reported sensitivity results, not improvements over v1's benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Equation (1) corrects the transmittance product to use alpha_k p_k instead of alpha_j p_j inside the product over k. This changes the mathematical expression meaningfully; the motion-model definitions in Appendix D remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and central benchmarking contribution remain intact. v2 removes the 'first clear snapshot' priority claim and adds an introduction-level claim of consistent TiNeuVox superiority, omitting the LPIPS exception still stated in Section 4.5.

C2.justification: Much of new Section 5 synthesizes existing interpretations. Substantive additions explain relative versus absolute NeRF-DS performance in Appendix A.2.5, interpret pose-noise artifacts as overfitting in B.3, and discuss computation, noise and domain-bias tradeoffs of additional supervision in Appendix F.

D1.justification: The public-release link changes from an anonymous website to the named MonoDyGauBench website, while direct links to pose-correction slides and a spreadsheet are removed. Section 3.1 newly states the split policy; the detailed hardware and implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix F substantially expands the research context beyond motion representations through a structured survey of smoothness and rigidity priors, optical flow, depth and tracking supervision. It connects these approaches to the benchmark's limitations and adds citations including Gao et al. (2024), Stearns et al. (2024), and Teed and Deng (2020).

P1.justification: v2 substantially expands the explanatory narrative through an eight-point introduction summary, a five-part discussion section and additional appendix discussions. It also changes the title, reorganizes the adaptive-density explanation and revises wording throughout, while retaining the original findings structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–11 and Figures 40–41. Existing figures are retained, with several relocated or resized, notably Figure 16; captions for Figures 36–39 are refined. Publication headers and local layout changes do not amount to a wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The controlled pose-noise study adds useful evidence beyond v1's real-data pose corrections, while the equation correction and expanded discussion improve precision and context. These gains are limited by an overbroad new TiNeuVox summary: unchanged Table 3, for example, favors DeformableGS. The added evidence and clarification provide a modest net improvement.
